links.outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education materials rewritten in plain language
links.effect: ChatGPT-4 lowered FKGL from 8.2 to 5.7 and raised FRE from 65.5 to 76.4; 29 of 41 (70.7%) articles were accurate without edits.
links.quote: The content of 29 (70.7%) articles was classified as “accurate” and required no additional revisions.

links.outcome: Content omissions and errors in ChatGPT-simplified articles as judged by orthopaedic trauma surgeons
links.effect: Three (7.3%) articles needed minor revisions and 9 (22%) needed major revisions; oversimplification was the most common error (58.3%).
links.quote: Nine (22%) articles were classified as “insufficient” and required major revisions (Table 3 ).

links.outcome: Expert surgeon review identifying content omissions in ChatGPT-revised patient education articles
links.effect: Expert review flagged 12 of 41 (29.3%) revised articles needing edits for omissions, oversimplification or loss of accuracy; 16 (39%) titles needed revision.
links.quote: However, nearly a third (29.3%) of the ChatGPT revised articles required revisions due to content omissions, thus highlighting the importance of expert review.

links.outcome: Reproducibility of ChatGPT output across repeated runs by two reviewers (ICC of FKGL/FRE)
links.effect: ICC 0.239 (95% CI −0.428 to 0.594) for FKGL and 0.607 (0.257–0.791) for FRE; different versions were produced for the same article with the same instructions.
links.quote: Indeed, comparing the generated texts between reviewers, 2 different versions were created for the same article despite using the same instructions.
The mean overall FKGL of the ChatGPT revised articles was significantly lower than the original OTA/AO articles (5.7 ± 0.5 vs. 8.2 ± 1.1, P < 0.001) (Fig. 1 ).

links.outcome: expert accuracy review of revised articles
links.effect: 29.3% required revisions due to omissions; 3 (7.3%) minor and 9 (22%) major revisions.
links.quote: However, nearly a third (29.3%) of the ChatGPT revised articles required revisions due to content omissions, thus highlighting the importance of expert review.

The readability of the ChatGPT revised articles measured by the 2 independent reviewers demonstrated poor interobserver agreement for the FKGL (ICC 0.239, 95% Confidence Interval [CI] −0.428 to 0.594) and moderate agreement for the FRE (ICC 0.607, 95% CI: 0.257–0.791).
